settings.heading: System settings
settings.intro: Values the system reads while running. They take effect without a redeployment; the Agent App picks up the PBX host at the next sign-in.
settings.rejected: Nothing was saved - check the fields marked in red.

pbx.host.label: PBX host (SIP)
pbx.host.hint: The address the Agent Apps register to over the VPN. Leave blank if it is not known yet.

agent.idle_logout_minutes.label: Automatic logout (minutes)
agent.idle_logout_minutes.hint: Laptops are shared between shifts, so the previous agent must not stay signed in.

agent.edit_window.label: Classification edit window
agent.edit_window.hint: How long an agent may edit the classification of their own calls.

sla.answer_seconds.label: Service level threshold (seconds)
sla.answer_seconds.hint: The percentage of calls answered within this time.

recording.retention_days.label: Recording retention (days)
recording.retention_days.hint: Recordings are deleted after this; the call record and classification remain.

reports.internal_numbers.label: Internal numbers
reports.internal_numbers.hint: The agents and branch extension numbers, comma separated. A call with one of these is recorded as usual but left out of the customer reports (S-48).

agent.call_log_days.label: Agent call log window (days)
agent.call_log_days.hint: How far back an agent can see their own calls. A week by default. Nothing is deleted - the contact history and your reports still show everything.

pos.lookup.interval_minutes.label: POS customer lookup, every (minutes)
pos.lookup.interval_minutes.hint: How often the server asks the POS about recent callers who are not in the contacts, and adds the ones it knows. 5 by default, 1 to 1440. Takes effect within half a minute.

pbx.heading: Abandoned calls from the PBX
pbx.intro: The server logs in to the PBX's web interface and downloads its Calls Detail report, then saves the calls marked Abandoned. Use a PBX user of its own, set to English, that can open Call Center reports.
pbx.urlHint: As you would open it in a browser, e.g. https://10.8.0.1. Leave blank to turn the import off.
pbx.passwordSet: A password is saved. Leave blank to keep it.
pbx.intervalHint: Between 1 and 60. Each check downloads from the day of the last successful one to today.
pbx.off: Not set up: the import is off.
pbx.never: Set up, not checked yet. The first check reaches back 30 days.

classification.heading: Classification form
classification.intro: The call types, and the questions an agent answers about each call.
classification.typesHint: Renaming is safe: reports are written against the stable key, not the label. A type in use can be hidden but not deleted.
classification.fieldsHint: Reorder with the arrows. Publishing creates a new version and leaves existing classifications alone.
classification.fieldsOutHint: Asked on calls an agent places. Its questions, and which of the call types above it offers, are its own.
classification.publishHint: Publishing creates a new version. Existing classifications keep the questions they were captured under, and a form that turns out wrong can be undone by publishing the old one again.
classification.unavailable: The form could not be loaded.

errors.bad_form: That form cannot be drawn. Every question needs a name and a kind, and there must be a call-type question.
errors.bad_name: A name is needed in both languages, and it must not already exist.
errors.type_in_use: Calls already use this type. Hide it instead of deleting it.
errors.server_unreachable: The server could not be reached.

classification.fieldsAppHint: Asked when an agent records a conversation from WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram or another app. Its questions, and which of the call types above it offers, are its own.
classification.typesOfferedHint: Untick a type to take it off this form. A new type joins a form only when ticked here, unless every box is ticked.
classification.typesOfferedKeepOne: A form must offer at least one type.

byChannel.title: Messages per channel
byChannel.hint: How many arrived on each app, and what they were about.

orders.title: Orders and order value
orders.hint: Orders taken through the apps and what they came to, grouped as you choose.

trend.title: Messages over time
trend.hint: Messages and orders per day, week, month, or hour of the day.

byAgent.title: Per agent
byAgent.hint: What each agent recorded, and how many were orders.

issues.title: Cancellations and complaints
issues.hint: The messages that went wrong, per channel.

channels.heading: Channels
channels.intro: The apps a customer can reach you on. Agents pick one when they record a message. Renaming is safe: messages keep the channel by its id.
channels.name: Name
channels.phoneHint: Built in: every call is filed under Phone, so it cannot be renamed or hidden.
channels.hiddenHint: A hidden channel is not offered to agents, but its messages stay in the history and the reports.

callReports.heading: Call reports
callReports.intro: The calls: how many, what they were about, who took them, and what went wrong. Calls only, except where a report compares the phone with the apps.
callReports.limited: Showing the first {{shown}} of {{total}}. Export CSV has them all.

summary.title: Communications
summary.hint: Calls and application messages in each period. Answered, missed and abandoned are incoming calls; missed counts missed and rejected, never an outgoing call nobody picked up. Abandoned calls come from the PBX, and their rings are not counted again. Internal calls are left out.

list.title: Every call, with all its details
list.hint: The full list is the Calls page: filter it there, then Export for every matching call.

byType.title: Calls per type
byType.hint: What the classified calls were about, and each type's share of them. Unclassified calls are not in the shares.

breakdown.title: Calls per day, agent or branch
breakdown.hint: Calls, answered and missed, and what they were about, grouped as you choose. An order is a call classified as Order.

byAgent.title: Calls per agent
byAgent.hint: What each agent's calls were: answered, missed, and their types.

recurring.title: Recurring customers
recurring.hint: Customers who called more than once in the period, most calls first. A number nobody saved is not a customer.

complaints.title: Complaints
complaints.hint: Every complaint call, newest first. Follow-up is the agent's tick; Resolved is set by a supervisor on the call.

complaintsBy.title: Complaints per branch and agent
complaintsBy.hint: How many, how many needed a follow-up and how many are resolved, the hours from the call to its resolution, and complaints per 100 orders.

repeat.title: Repeat complainers
repeat.hint: Customers who complained more than once in the period.

peakHours.title: Peak hours
peakHours.hint: Incoming calls in each hour of each weekday, for staffing: the stronger the blue, the busier. Calls the agents made are not demand and are not counted.

ordersByChannel.title: Orders by channel
ordersByChannel.hint: Phone against each app: how many orders, what they came to, and each channel's share of all orders.

ordersTrend.title: Orders over time, phone and apps
ordersTrend.hint: Orders taken by phone and through the apps in each day, week or month.

orderValue.title: Order value
orderValue.hint: Total and average order value, phone and apps together, grouped as you choose. A cancellation with a value on it is not revenue.

cancellations.title: Cancellation rate
cancellations.hint: Cancellations against orders, phone and apps together, per branch, channel or agent.

cancellationList.title: Cancellations, with their notes
cancellationList.hint: Every cancellation in the period, newest first, by phone or through an app.

customerBase.title: New and returning customers
customerBase.hint: Customers who called in each period. New means first saved in that period; the customers carried over from the old system count as returning.

topCustomers.title: Top customers
topCustomers.hint: The 50 customers with the most orders, or the most order value, in the period.

inactive.title: Customers to win back
inactive.hint: Customers who have ordered before but not in the last days you choose, counted back from today over every order they ever placed — not only the period above.

productivity.title: Agent productivity
productivity.hint: Per agent: calls handled (answered, in and out), average talk time over answered calls, orders and their value, answered calls left unclassified, and missed calls on their extension - every ring they did not take, the rings of abandoned calls included.

missed.title: Missed calls
missed.hint: Incoming calls missed, rejected or abandoned in the queue, and their share of all incoming calls. The rings of an abandoned call count once, as the abandoned call. An outgoing call nobody picked up is not a missed call.

missedList.title: Every missed call
missedList.hint: Newest first, with the note the agent left on it. An abandoned call has no agent.

quality.title: Data quality
quality.hint: What is missing or doubtful in the period. Unclassified calls can be found on the Calls page with Classified: No.

unknownNumbers.title: Numbers nobody saved
unknownNumbers.hint: Numbers that called or were called and are not on any contact, most calls first.

duplicateNames.title: Names shared by more than one contact
duplicateNames.hint: Contacts with the same name, however it is spelt. A shared name is a question, not a mistake: common names are common. Merging two contacts is not built yet (A-63). Not limited to the period.

abandoned.title: Abandoned calls
abandoned.hint: Callers who gave up waiting in the queue before anybody took the call, from the PBX's own report: how many, their share of incoming calls, how long they waited, and how many were called back. Grouped as you choose.

abandonedList.title: Every abandoned call
abandonedList.hint: Newest first. Waited is time in the queue; Rings is how often an agent's phone rang with the call. Called back is the first call anybody made to the number after the caller hung up.

quality.duplicateNames: Names shared by more than one contact
